mechanism: Non-internalized VEGF-targeted antibody-drug conjugate using MediLink's TMALIN tumor-microenvironment-activable linker-payload platform; YL242 combines an anti-VEGF antibody, protease-cleavable tripeptide linker, and DNA topoisomerase I inhibitor payload C24 intended to release extracellularly in the tumor microenvironment.
development_status: Recruiting first-in-human, multicenter, open-label Phase 1/2 study in advanced solid tumors; ClinicalTrials.gov lists actual study start on 2025-09-22, estimated primary completion in 2028-09, estimated study completion in 2028-11, and no posted results.
clinical_summary: NCT07197827 is an estimated 424-participant, non-randomized Phase 1/2 trial testing YL242 monotherapy and combinations with pembrolizumab and/or 5-FU/LV in advanced solid tumors. Primary measures include ORR for expansion parts and treatment-emergent adverse events; expansion cohorts include advanced solid tumors plus selected NSCLC, HCC, mCRC, and HER2-negative gastric/GEJ populations. No human efficacy data were found as of this review.
safety_summary: Human safety is not yet characterized. The trial makes TEAEs a primary outcome and excludes patients with prior intolerance to topoisomerase I inhibitor ADCs, clinically significant cardiovascular/cerebrovascular disease, clinically significant pulmonary disease, and leptomeningeal disease. Preclinical AACR data reported promising non-human-primate safety with no drug-related adverse effects, but analog topoisomerase I ADCs support monitoring for ILD/pneumonitis, myelosuppression, GI toxicity, and cardiac/LVEF concerns.
management_tools: Compendia and label-concordance review at launch
evidence_gaps: No published human efficacy or safety results for YL242 were found.
No registrational trial, pivotal indication, biomarker-defined population, or regulatory filing timeline was identified.
YL242 dose, treatment duration, and commercial price are not established.
Combination regimens with pembrolizumab and/or 5-FU/LV could materially change total regimen cost and utilization controls.

sources.title: Abstract 3140: Preclinical development of YL242, a non-internalized antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) targeting soluble VEGF for treatment of solid tumors
supports: YL242 is a non-internalized ADC targeting soluble VEGF.
YL242 incorporates an anti-VEGF antibody, protease-cleavable tripeptide linker, and DNA topoisomerase I inhibitor payload.

Preclinical results reported dose-dependent antitumor effects, complete tumor regressions in xenograft models, plasma stability, and no drug-related adverse effects in pivotal non-human-primate toxicity studies.

sources.title: ENHERTU (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) Prescribing Information
supports: Enhertu is a marketed antibody and topoisomerase inhibitor conjugate used as an ADC pricing/safety analog.
Recommended dosing includes 5.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks for breast, NSCLC, and HER2-positive solid tumors and 6.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks for gastric/GEJ cancer.
Label includes warnings for ILD/pneumonitis, neutropenia, left ventricular dysfunction, and embryo-fetal toxicity.

sources.title: Enhertu (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) Prior Authorization Criteria
supports: Analog ADC policy uses six-month initial authorization with renewal based on disease response and absence of unacceptable toxicity.
Policy applies quantity limits and max units per 21-day cycle and requires LVEF monitoring.
Policy lists HCPCS J9358 as 1 billable unit per 1 mg.

sources.title: J9358 Medicare Reimbursement Rate (2026)
supports: Reports Q2 2026 Medicare national average payment of $31.26 per 1 mg for J9358, injection fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki.
Used as a current marketed ADC analog for YL242 annual drug acquisition cost because YL242 has no commercial price.

expected_launch_window.method: Estimated from current Phase 1/2 recruiting status, no results, estimated primary completion in 2028-09, and typical oncology progression through expansion/pivotal study plus regulatory review.
expected_launch_window.explanation: No company launch guidance was found. Earliest plausible launch is several years after the 2028 primary completion if efficacy supports accelerated or pivotal development.

annual_cost_range.method: Used marketed topoisomerase-I ADC Enhertu as analog: 5.4-6.4 mg/kg every 3 weeks for a 70 kg patient equals about 6,552-7,765 mg/year; multiplied by $31.26 per mg Q2 2026 J9358 payment produces about $205k-$243k before administration, wastage, and combination-drug costs, rounded to $200k-$250k.
annual_cost_range.explanation: YL242 has no price and dose is not established, so this is an analog drug-acquisition estimate only. Pembrolizumab or chemotherapy combinations could raise total regimen cost.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced novel VEGF-targeted, non-internalized ADC mechanism and preclinical antitumor activity against lack of human efficacy/safety data.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Mechanism is differentiated versus traditional internalizing ADCs and VEGF antibodies, but clinical differentiation remains unproven until human response and safety results are available.

budget_impact.method: Rated from high analog ADC per-patient cost, potential broad solid-tumor scope, but low near-term utilization because the asset is Phase 1/2 and unapproved.
budget_impact.explanation: If later positioned broadly across common solid tumors or in combination with pembrolizumab, budget impact could move higher.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from early clinical stage, no human results, and launch window likely beyond 2030.
disruption_risk.explanation: Near-term payer disruption is limited to monitoring; risk could rise after expansion data or a registrational cohort is disclosed.

recommended_action.method: Pipeline action matched to Phase 1/2 recruiting asset with no posted human efficacy or safety results.
recommended_action.explanation: Track initial dose-escalation/expansion readouts, biomarker strategy, registrational plans, and combination use before moving to active policy planning.

quality_flags: No direct YL242 commercial price; cost range uses Enhertu analog dosing and Q2 2026 J9358 payment.
AACR evidence is preclinical and company-authored; no independent peer-reviewed human YL242 data found.
ClinicalTrials.gov page is last updated 2025-12-24 and lists no results.
